title: Status line hides the git segment on a detached HEAD
story: A session opened on a detached HEAD, such as a worktree made from a commit or a tag, used to lose its whole git segment, so the line looked as if the folder were outside git. Now the segment names the commit, for example [detached:27bbbf1], and still shows the stashed, untracked, modified and unpushed counts. Branches and folders outside git look exactly as before.

checks.criterion: On a detached HEAD, the first line shows [detached:<short commit id>] followed by the four state words.
checks.steps: mkdir -p /tmp/qa-sl/h && git -C /tmp/qa-sl init -q -b main repo && git -C /tmp/qa-sl/repo commit -q --allow-empty -m first; git -C /tmp/qa-sl/repo checkout -q --detach && touch /tmp/qa-sl/repo/new.txt; printf '{"cwd":"/tmp/qa-sl/repo"}' | HOME=/tmp/qa-sl/h bash baselines/statusline/statusline.sh | head -1
checks.expected: [detached:<id>]  | stashed:0 untracked:1 modified:0 unpushed:0, where <id> matches git -C /tmp/qa-sl/repo rev-parse --short HEAD.

checks.criterion: On a branch the segment is exactly as before, and outside a repository there is no git segment.
checks.steps: git -C /tmp/qa-sl init -q -b main repo2 && git -C /tmp/qa-sl/repo2 commit -q --allow-empty -m first && mkdir -p /tmp/qa-sl/plain; pipe {"cwd":"/tmp/qa-sl/repo2"} and then {"cwd":"/tmp/qa-sl/plain"} into the script with HOME=/tmp/qa-sl/h, keeping the first line.
checks.expected: repo2 shows [main]  | stashed:0 untracked:0 modified:0 unpushed:0; plain shows ctx: -- then only the cost, with no [...] and no stashed:.
